prerequisites: Engineering science fundamentals of Bachelor's degree

learning_outcomes.text: Students have the basic knowledge and understanding of product cost management in product development. They have integrated basic knowledge about developing safety- and ergonomics-compliant products. Students know the essential connections between regulations, directives, and standards and know how to apply them.

Students are aware of the very large cost responsibility of product development. They can reduce life cycle costs, prime costs, and manufacturing costs using Target Costing methods. Students can calculate the prime costs of a product. With their knowledge, they can design products ergonomically and safely, including with the help of computer-aided methods, with regard to the product's intended use. Students can confidently select and apply the correct EU directives and regulations. They can carry out a complete certification according to the CE marking legally prescribed by the EU.

Students carry out a complete CE certification process for various practical examples. They identify relevant applicable directives and regulations and implement them. They analyze hazards, conduct a risk analysis and risk assessment. Appropriate safety-related solutions are developed and implemented for all analyzed hazards. Students establish a reference to valid standards for all essential work steps. Students analyze their implemented solution with regard to ergonomic usability using computer-based methods and revise their solution with the aim of designing a safe and user-friendly product. The practical, legal, and social relevance of the topics is demonstrated using researched accidents and non-ergonomically designed products. Students learn in project groups to critically analyze complex problems, develop common solutions, and present and defend them. Students can participate in standard tasks for optimizing product costs. They can carry out a complete CE certification in accordance with the laws and standards applicable in the EU.
Graduates can interpret safety-related standards and regulations and apply them to real practical examples.
Students independently review and critically question self-constructed solutions.
Students can present their work results orally and in writing in a clearly structured form. Students can independently discuss problems in a group, reach a decision, and present and defend it.
Students can independently recognize safety-critical issues, professionally justify them factually, and find solutions.

syllabus_topics: EU directives & regulations in the context of product safety
Hazards and risks in work systems
Influence of loads on the human body
Simulation of human-machine interaction - Motion tracking and Virtual Reality
Target price and product costs in product development
Benefit and value of a product from the customer's perspective
Fundamentals of cost accounting and calculation of product-related costs
Measures in product development to save costs

assessment_methods.method: Presentation: Analysis of hazards, safety concept
Exam (K0.5): Price and costs of products

assessment_rules: The portfolio exam is graded using a point system, with a maximum of 100 points achievable. The exam consists of three presentations and one written exam (K0.5). The first two presentations can achieve a maximum of 25 points each, the third presentation a maximum of 35 points, and the K0.5 exam a maximum of 15 points.
